newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi customs workers call off strike.
newsitem.headline: Malawi customs workers call off strike.

text.p: Malawi's customs workers union called off a strike planned for Tuesday to avoid confrontation with management and the police, a senior union official said.

The union's 400 members, who generate more than 80 percent of government's total revenue, threatened to join a month-long strike by workers in other government departments demanding a 100 percent wage increase.

The secretary general of the union, Honeck Kampini, told Reuters on Tuesday the union decided to call off the strike to avoid direct confrontation with police after government deployed senior officers to all strategic stations and put police on alert.
"When we read this letter that they've sent officers to all stations, we knew there would be direct confrontation. We have decided to call off the strike," Kampini said.
Finance and Economic Planning Minister Aleke Banda said on Monday the government would use all possible means to ensure all customs posts were working, to avoid crippling the economy.

The government is refusing to grant the 100,000-strong civil service the 100 percent increase, saying it would destabilise the economy, which grew by more than nine percent in 1996 and is projected to grow a further seven percent this year. Instead, it has offered to increase wages by 47 percent.
Malawi's lowest-paid workers earn on average $20 per month.
